newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK must act to keep services competitive - industry.
newsitem.headline: HK must act to keep services competitive - industry.

text.p: Wealthy Hong Kong should consider cutting taxes, and improving its English skills, to stave off regional rivals, according to the Hong Kong Coalition of Service Industries (HKCSI).

"I think it's fair to say that an important element in Hong Kong's success has been its continued recognition as a low cost tax centre from which to do business," HKCSI chairman Brian Stevenson told an American Chamber of Commerce luncheon.

But over the years, Hong Kong's competition -- particularly those within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations region -- had aggressively cut taxes and offered incentives to attract overseas investors, he said.
"From the viewpoint of competitiveness, the government should look very carefully at reducing base rates of taxation," Stevenson said.
Stevenson said having the most competitive tax regime in the region was not good enough. "We have -- that is a statement of fact -- but we must challenge ourselves to do even better."
He said the territory had "tremendous" financial reserves to fund such a cut.
According to government figures, Hong Kong had US$63.8 billion in foreign reserves at the end of March, making it one of the wealthiest places in the world on a per capita basis.
Stevenson said Hong Kong could cut taxes further.
"We're not talking of anything absolutely radical," he said, suggesting a cut in corporate tax rates to 15 percent from 16.5 percent.
He also said Hong Kong must maintain its English skills

"English skills are critically important for Hong Kong and the future," he said. "If they deteriorate -- and I believe there is concern they are deteriorating - then we could lose out to our colleagues in the region."
